\section[jvaraḥ]{\sk{ज्वरः} (jvaraḥ) — a fever}

\label{lesson:SA-C66-fever}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for second, then the Sanskrit for first.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{ज्वरः}}
\textbf{\sk{ज्वरः}} (\emph{jvaraḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a fever\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\sk{मम} \sk{ज्वरः} \sk{अस्ति}} (\emph{mama jvaraḥ asti}) — \textquotedblleft{}I have a fever\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}of me a fever is\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\sk{मम}} and \textbf{\sk{अस्ति}}, which you know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An illness, said with of-me and is.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jvaraḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jvaraḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mama jvaraḥ asti}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for second, then the Sanskrit for first, then say \emph{jvaraḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{ज्वरः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fever\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[ārogyam]{\sk{आरोग्यम्} (ārogyam) — health}

\label{lesson:SA-C66-health}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for pain, then the Sanskrit for an illness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{आरोग्यम्}}
\textbf{\sk{आरोग्यम्}} (\emph{ārogyam}) — \textquotedblleft{}health\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\sk{आ}-}, then \textbf{\sk{रोग}}, \textquotedblleft{}illness\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{-\sk{य}} after it — the state of the body once the illness is gone.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
What you wish someone who is ill.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ārogyam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ārogyam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ārogyam astu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for pain, then the Sanskrit for an illness, then say \emph{ārogyam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
